questions.qtext: Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?

options.text: The loss of available energy is more, when heat loss occurs at lower temperature than when the same heat loss occurs at a higher temperature.
The exergy of a fluid at a higher temperature is more than that at a lower temperature.
Exergy of an isolated system may or may not be conserved.
The exergy of an isolated system can never decrease.

questions.solution:
(b, c)
• The loss of available energy is more, when heat loss occurs at a higher temperature than when the same heat loss occurs at a lower temperature.
• While energy is always conserved, exergy is not generally conserved, but is destroyed by irreversibilities.
• The exergy of an isolated system can never increase.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT?

options.text: The entropy of an isolated system always decreases and becomes a minimum at the state of equilibrium.
If an isentropic process is reversible, it must be adiabatic.
Entropy generation is a point or state function.
There is no entropy transfer associated with work transfer.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
• The entropy of an isolated system always increases and becomes a maximum at the state of equilibrium.
• Entropy is a point or state function but entropy generation is a path function.
• There is no entropy transfer associated with work transfer, even if work is dissipated adiabatically into internal energy increase of the system, there is an entropy increase in the system, but there is as such no entropy transfer to it.
